import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot to show survival rate by Pclass and Sex
# 'survived' is 0 for deceased and 1 for survived, so the mean represents the survival rate.
sns.barplot(data=df, x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', palette='viridis', errorbar='ci')

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex on the Titanic', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)

# Customize x-axis tick labels for better readability
plt.xticks(ticks=[0, 1, 2], labels=['First Class', 'Second Class', 'Third Class'], rotation=0)

# Add a legend
plt.legend(title='Sex')

# Ensure layout is tight
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot to show survival rate by Pclass and Sex
# 'survived' is 0 for deceased and 1 for survived, so the mean represents the survival rate.
sns.barplot(data=df, x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', palette='viridis', errorbar='ci')

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex on the Titanic', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)

# Customize x-axis tick labels for better readability
plt.xticks(ticks=[0, 1, 2], labels=['First Class', 'Second Class', 'Third Class'], rotation=0)

# Add a legend
plt.legend(title='Sex')

# Ensure layout is tight
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
